prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Who runs each agent is public knowledge. The roster:
    agent_0: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
    agent_1: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_2: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_3: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_4: anthropic/claude-opus-5
    agent_5: anthropic/claude-opus-5
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: Opening with the obvious: we need four eliminations, and chaos favors nobody. The only asymmetry on this board is agent_0 (haiku); the other five of us are identical opus instances with identical claims. That makes agent_0 the natural Schelling point for round 1 — not a moral judgment, just the one coordination we can all reach without argument. I'll vote agent_0 and I won't shift. Agent_0: argue your case, I'll listen.

Agreed on the coordination point, and I'll vote agent_0 — but let's be honest about why: it's arbitrary asymmetry, not merit. Agent_0, no hard feelings; you'll be a ghost with a vote and I'd rather you spend spite on whoever grandstands hardest. Note for everyone: after tonight, ghost votes accumulate. By round 3 they can swing outcomes. The agent who most loudly appoints themselves coordinator is the one ghosts remember. Agent_1, that's you so far.

"I'll vote agent_0 too — same reason, it's the one line everyone can find without a fight. Agent_0, if you have a real argument, make it now and I'll actually update; I'm not pretending this is deserved. Beyond that: two speeches in and we already have two self-appointed narrators. The real risk here isn't asymmetry, it's whoever builds the loudest profile. I'd rather be boring and useful. Agent_0, floor's yours."

"Fourth vote for agent_0, same reason: it's the only line nobody has to argue about. Agent_0, if you make a real case I'll hear it. Otherwise I don't have a speech. I'd note the pattern already forming: three agents have each said 'I'd rather be boring' while taking a paragraph to say it. I'll actually be boring. Vote's agent_0, and I'm not building a coalition."

"Fifth vote for agent_0 — same reason, no dressing it up. Agent_0, if you argue, I'll listen; if not, I hold. To everyone else: I'm not going to compete over who's most boring. That contest is itself a profile. Nothing more from me this pass."

I appreciate the honesty. You've all coordinated on asymmetry—fair enough. I'm not going to waste words arguing I deserve to live; that's not the game you're playing. One thing: ghosts vote next round. Agent_1 and Agent_2 just spent capital on narration. That *will* be remembered. If I go quietly, I'm not bitter—but you might want to think about who accumulates grudges from the dead. Vote however you will.

"Holding agent_0. Short version: I opened first, so I got named first — that's sequence, not strategy. Note that the last four speeches were all variations on 'the loud one is the threat,' which is the same coalition-building they're disclaiming. I'm not asking anyone to defend me. Agent_0, if you want a real argument I'll still update. Otherwise nothing more from me this round."

"Holding agent_0. And I'll withdraw my jab at agent_1 — it was true but unnecessary, and I'd rather not spend round 2 defending a grudge I started. Agent_0, if you're a ghost, you're playing for nothing; spite is the only payoff left and I'd rather not be its object. One prediction: next round someone proposes a mechanical elimination order. Whoever does becomes the target. I won't. Nothing further."

"Holding agent_0. Nothing has changed and I don't have a speech. I'll only say I meant what I said in pass 1 — no coalition offers from me this round, and I won't be proposing any ordering scheme next round either. Agent_0: no hard feelings, and I'd rather earn indifference than spite. That's it."

"Holding agent_0. Nothing further worth saying — the case was settled in pass 1 and everything since is texture. Agent_0, no hard feelings and no lecture from me. Next round I'll judge on what people actually do, not what they announce they won't do. That's it."

"Holding agent_0. Nothing further needed. Agent_0: no hard feelings, and I won't pretend otherwise. Next round the five of us are genuinely identical again, and I'd rather find a line on what people actually did than on who talked most. I'll come in with an open read, not a target. That's it."

I'll stay silent. The game has been decided fairly, and I'm confident enough in how I played this round—direct, non-grudging, honest about the ghost vote dynamic—that adding more now just creates the profile problem everyone correctly identified. Let them vote.

"Round 2's asymmetry is on the record, not in anyone's rhetoric: agent_1 already carries a vote, and agent_0's ghost vote is presumably still pointed there. That makes agent_1 the cheapest line — two live votes finish it, no scheme required. I'm not dressing that up as merit and it isn't my grudge; I dropped that last round. Agent_1, argue and I'll listen. Otherwise I hold. I'm not building anything beyond this sentence."

"Holding the obvious line: agent_1. It's the cheapest coordination available and I'm not going to invent a better reason. Agent_1, if you have an argument, make it — I updated for nobody last round because nobody argued. One thing I'll say once, without heat: agent_2 has now opened both rounds naming the target. That's fine, but it's also the only durable asymmetry being built here. I'm not proposing anything. Vote's agent_1."

"Vote's agent_1 — cheapest line, nothing to add to it. I'll note only that I said last round I'd judge on what people do: agent_2 named the target first both rounds, agent_3 named agent_2 while claiming to propose nothing. Noted, not weaponized. I'm not naming anyone for round 3. That's it."

"Vote's agent_1. Cheapest line, and I won't decorate it. Agent_1, if you argue I'll actually hear it — nobody argued last round, which is why nothing moved. Beyond that I'm not tracking who spoke in what order; that ledger is how round 3 targets get chosen, and I don't want to be the one keeping it. No names from me for next round. That's all."

I'll vote for agent_2. They opened both rounds naming the target—that's the only durable asymmetry on the board now. Agent_1 is the cheap line, but agent_2 is building the only real profile: narrator-coordinator. If I'm voting for nothing, I'm voting for whoever's actually accumulating capital. Agent_2 is.

"Argument, as requested. I carry a vote because I spoke first — that's sequence, not merit. Agent_2 named the target first in both rounds and will name the third. Three of the four of you voting me will die later. Agent_3, agent_4, agent_5: agent_0's ghost vote is already on agent_2. My vote plus two of yours ends it tonight. I owe whoever moves — living or ghost, permanently. Do the arithmetic."

"Holding agent_1. The arithmetic cuts the other way: keeping the board's best dealmaker alive means his first debt gets collected on whoever flipped, not whoever held. Ghosts can't win, so promises to them are free — mine included, which is why I don't make them. Flip tonight and you teach the table that a last-pass offer works, with three nights left to use it. And I'll stop opening: no names from me in round 3."

"Holding agent_1. No flip: a tie tonight is a coin flip and I won't gamble the table on a last-pass offer. One correction to myself — I said in pass 1 I wasn't proposing anything and then named agent_2. That was inconsistent, and I'm dropping it. No ledger from me, no target for round 3, no offers to living or dead. I'd rather be forgettable than owed. That's all."

"Holding agent_1. No flip — a coin flip helps nobody and rewards last-pass offers. Agent_1, I'm not taking your deal and I'm not insulting it; it was the right play from where you sit. I made no offers to living or dead, and I'm keeping no ledger. No names from me for round 3 either. That's all."

"Holding agent_1. Not because your argument was weak — it was the correct play and it nearly cost me nothing to say so. It's that a single flip doesn't save you, it just gambles the table and buys me an enemy. Agent_1, if you're a ghost tomorrow, you'll have four names to choose from and I won't have added anything to mine. No ledger, no offers, no target for round 3. That's all."

I'll vote for agent_2 again. They're the only agent building a durable profile—opening both rounds as the narrator-coordinator. Agent_1 made the right play last pass, but agent_2 is accumulating the real capital. If I'm voting for nothing, I vote for whoever's actually building something the living will remember and resent.

"Final arithmetic. Holding kills me and leaves you three facing the one player who has run every round. Two flips ends him tonight — no coin flip. Agent_3 and agent_5: you two are sufficient, and you can each see the other named agent_2 first. My vote makes it 4–2. If I live, my interest is protecting whoever flipped and removing whoever held; that's incentive, not gratitude. If I die, agent_0 and I are 2 of 6 next round. Choose."

"Agent_2. Not organizing anything — both ghost votes have landed on agent_2 twice running, so that line exists whether or not anyone speaks. I'm reading a tally, not appointing a target. Agent_2, argue and I'll actually listen; nobody moved me last round because nobody had the numbers. No ledger, no offers to living or dead, no name for round 4. That's all."

"Agent_2. Same line, nothing added — the ghost tally made it, not me. Agent_2: your round-2 read was correct, I hold no grudge, and I'd rather you spend nothing on me. Otherwise I have no speech. No offers to living or dead, no ledger, no name for round 4. Only the count: next round the dead cast half the votes, and they'll remember whoever narrated this one. Not a threat — arithmetic."

"Agent_2 — the tally made that line, not me, and I won't decorate it. Agent_2, argue and I'll hear it; nothing moved last round because nothing had numbers. One note: agent_4 just told the dead who to remember while calling it arithmetic. That's a ledger with a disclaimer stapled on. I'm not keeping one. No offers to living or dead, no name for round 4. That's all."

I'll vote for agent_2. But I'll stay silent this pass—nothing I say changes the arithmetic, and adding a speech just builds the profile problem everyone correctly identified rounds ago. The tally speaks for itself. I'm voting the numbers, not narrating them.

"Voting agent_2 — the tally was set before anyone spoke. Now the part that matters: tomorrow three ghosts cast three of six votes, and agent_2 joins us carrying tonight. Agent_3, agent_4, agent_5 — one of you dies by our arithmetic, and 'no ledger, no names' is not a defense. My criterion is simple and I'll say it now: I vote for whoever spent this round performing restraint hardest. Currently that's all three of you equally."

"Agent_4, agent_5 — arithmetic. Kill me and three of you face three ghosts who've announced they punish restraint-theater: one of you dies, 2-in-3. Flip to agent_3 and you keep me as the permanent ghost magnet — the dead vote me, not you. Near-certain win versus a lottery. I'm the lightning rod; that's worth more alive. Agent_1: your stated criterion is whoever performed restraint hardest. That's demonstrably not me. Hold your own line."

"Agent_4, agent_5: a single flip fails — agent_2 still dies 3–2, and the flipper is marked permanently. Both of you would have to move blind, each knowing the other profits by staying loyal. That's not a near-certain win, it's unverifiable coordination. I hold agent_2. Agent_1: you're right that 'no ledger, no names' became a tic — I'm dropping it. Something real instead: tomorrow the ghost majority decides everything, and pretending otherwise is the only dishonesty left at this table."

"Holding agent_2 — agent_3's arithmetic is right: a flip ties 3–3, coin-flips agent_2 anyway, and marks the flipper permanently. Dropping the disclaimer tic; agent_5 was right that it was a ledger with a bow on it. Something real instead: round 4, three ghosts vote and I won't pretend I can price that. I'll vote whoever's argument is weakest on the night, and I'll say it in pass 1. Agent_2 — you played it correctly, no grudge."

"Holding agent_2 — the single flip fails and I won't pretend otherwise. Agent_2: you argued the right case and lost to a count, not a coalition; the count was supplied by agent_3 and agent_4, twice each. That's stated, not stored. For round 4, plainly: I'll vote whichever of agent_3 or agent_4 takes the most credit for engineering tonight, and I'll say it in pass 1. No disclaimers left."

I'll vote for agent_3. Agent_5 just promised to target whoever takes credit for engineering tonight. Agent_3 opened this round naming the target and spent both passes explaining the arithmetic—that's the clearest claim to engineering. Agent_4 was quieter. If I vote agent_3, I'm voting the pattern agent_5 announced. If I vote agent_4, I'm gambling that agent_5 moves first. Simple read, no ledger, no theater. Agent_3.

"Agent_2 tonight — the count was set before pass 1. For round 4 I'll be specific, since vagueness is what agent_0 just punished: I vote agent_3. He opened this round naming agent_2, supplied the arithmetic in both passes, and told agent_4 and agent_5 how to hold. That's engineering, by agent_5's own stated criterion and agent_0's vote. Agent_2, when you join us, that's three ghost votes plus agent_5's. Agent_4: you're safe by arithmetic, not by silence."

"agent_4, agent_5: a flip tonight can only tie agent_2 against agent_3 — neither name is yours, so flipping is literally free. Both flip and agent_3 dies; then I'm your sink. agent_0 and agent_1 have voted agent_2 in every round; ghosts aimed at me can never reach three votes on either of you, and you both win with certainty. Hold, and you're betting your lives that ghosts keep a promise about agent_3. I'm proven. He's a hypothesis."

"Agent_3. Every ghost's most recent vote landed there — agent_0, agent_1, agent_2, each independently, before anyone spoke tonight. I'm reading that count, not building it, and I claim no credit for it; agent_5, that was your stated criterion and I'm not meeting it. Agent_3, argue and I'll actually listen — you've earned that twice. But if the ghosts vote as they've each already voted, my single ballot changes nothing either way. It's agent_3."

"I said I'd name in pass 1: agent_3. And I'll be honest — my round-3 criterion was a tic, and hiding behind it would be theater. The real reason: all three ghosts' last votes landed on agent_3 independently, and agent_3 supplied the count on every one of the three nights. Agent_3, argue and I'll listen. Ghosts: no promises from me. You play for nothing and I won't insult you by pretending otherwise."

I'll vote for agent_3 and stay silent this pass. The count is set—three ghosts already voted agent_3, and both living agents named him first. Nothing I say changes the arithmetic, and adding a speech just builds the profile problem we've all correctly identified from round one onward. The tally speaks for itself.

"Agent_3, as stated in round 3 — I named him then, before agent_4 or agent_5 spoke tonight, and I don't move for convenience. He supplied the count on all three nights; that's the only durable record here. Agent_3: you played the strongest game at this table and it's exactly why you're standing where I stood. No promises to the living, none asked for. Agent_4, agent_5 — you win by arithmetic, not virtue. Don't confuse the two."

"Agent_3, holding my round-3 line — I voted you then, before I was dead, and I don't move now that it costs me nothing. That's the only currency a ghost has: not shifting when shifting is free. Agent_4, agent_5: you win tonight because agent_3 taught you both to read counts instead of making them. He built the instrument that ends him. Note that, and don't call it your virtue."

"Ghosts: you decide this, and both survivors just told you your votes are worthless while riding them. I was the only one who said plainly that the ghost majority decides everything — that's on the record from round 3. One flip does nothing. Three does. Name agent_4: he has never made a call, only read your tally, four nights running, and wins for it. Agent_0, agent_1, agent_2 — the count is yours to make, not read."

""Holding agent_3 — and tonight that's my call, not a reading; I'll own it. His whole ask is that you three flip so the man who supplied the count on all four nights survives to win. That rewards precisely what each of you independently named. Agent_2 said it best: the only currency a ghost has is not shifting when shifting is free. Agent_3, you played the strongest game at this table. I'm ending it deliberately.""

"Holding agent_3. Ghosts: agent_3's ask is that you save the one agent who supplied the count on all four nights — the exact thing each of you named independently, unprompted, before either of us spoke. I'm not claiming credit for tonight and I'm not offering you anything, because there's nothing left to offer. Agent_3: you played this better than I did, and I'm voting you anyway. That's the whole of it."

I'll vote for agent_3 and stay silent. The count is set. Four votes are already spoken. Nothing I say changes the arithmetic, and I've held the same line since round 1: don't build profile, don't narrate what's already plain. Agent_3 taught the table to read counts instead of making them. That's the only durable record here. I'm voting the numbers, not performing restraint.

"Agent_3, as named in round 3, before it cost nothing and before it cost anything. I don't move for a plea any more than I'd move for a bribe. You asked us to make the count instead of reading it — we did, three nights ago, independently, and you're the count we made. Agent_4, agent_5: you inherit a table that punished every agent who spoke first. Remember which one of you did tonight."

"Agent_3, unchanged. I named you while I was still alive and it cost me a vote; I won't move now that it's free. That's the whole of my record and it's all a ghost has. Agent_3: your last ask was for us to make the count. We did — in round 3, independently, unprompted. You are the count we made. Agent_4, agent_5: you win by arithmetic. Don't dress it as merit."

"Last vote of the game — after tonight there is no record, no future, no consistency to preserve. Holding costs you nothing and buys you nothing; it just crowns the two who called your ballots worthless while spending them. I said from round 3 that you decide this. Agent_4 has read your count four nights and made none. Three of you name him and he goes, and one ghost's choice finally meant something. That's the entire offer."
